candidates.buyer: Small foundations, corporations, NGOs, church and community bodies that handle funds (volunteer treasurers)
candidates.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
candidates.evidence: https://www.primicias.ec/economia/obligaciones-organizaciones-sociales-ecuador-riesgo-108374/ ; https://www.ecija.com/actualidad-insights/ley-de-transparencia-social-establece-nuevas-obligaciones-para-organizaciones-en-ecuador/ ; https://nmslaw.com.ec/blog/2025/09/01/ley-organica-transparencia-social-ecuador/ ; https://www.eldiario.ec/ecuador/ley-de-transparencia-social-ya-esta-vigente-tras-publicacion-en-registro-oficial-28082025/ . Hivos notes the risk-based rules are hard for small bodies.
candidates.existing: Law-firm and consultancy notes only (NMSLaw, ECIJA). I found no dedicated software, but the competitor search was limited to one query.
candidates.known_note: Different buyer (non-profits, not savings banks) and different regulator duty, though the SEPS regulates both.
candidates.name: Transparency-law compliance pack for small foundations, corporations and community associations (SUIOS registration, risk-tier reports, 30-day director updates)
candidates.trigger: Ley Orgánica de Transparencia Social (Registro Oficial 28 Aug 2025) and its general regulation (Decreto Ejecutivo 191, Oct 2025). Registration in SUIOS within 180 days of publication, which would be about late Feb 2026 (my own calculation, not confirmed). SEPS risk tiers: low risk files a simplified report every 2 years and updates directors within 30 days. Medium risk files an annual report plus yearly financial statements reviewed by an independent accountant within 3 months of year end. High risk files an annual report plus audited statements and runs an integrity system. Late or incomplete filing is sanctioned, up to suspension or loss of legal personality. Six unconstitutionality suits had been filed by Oct 2025; outcome unchecked.
candidates.unchecked: Number of organisations, actual 2026 deadlines and any extension, Constitutional Court outcome, whether SUIOS is free and easy, whether the risk-tier criteria exclude most small bodies, local competitor search such as 'software + SUIOS + fundaciones'.

candidates.buyer: Juntas administradoras de agua potable y saneamiento; rural and peri-urban community boards (Quito alone has 94)
candidates.evidence: https://www.primicias.ec/quito/municipio-cobro-tasa-recoleccion-basura-juntas-agua-comunitario-dmq-reclamo-legal-117235/ ; https://www.gob.ec/sites/default/files/sign/procedure-MAE-036-01-01-20260808171717-20205140-signed.pdf ; https://www.asambleanacional.gob.ec/es/node/116849 . Exact periodic reporting duty to ARCA is unverified.
candidates.existing: None found, but I did not run a competitor search.
candidates.name: Tariff-costing and compliance helper for community drinking-water boards (juntas administradoras de agua)
candidates.trigger: ARCA Guía de Costos for water and sanitation service, approved in Registro Oficial 756 (March 2025). ARCA says juntas must charge values calculated to cover operation, maintenance and treatment. Boards also need legal personality from the environment ministry (procedure updated Sept 2025). The Quito municipality wants to add the waste fee to their billing.
candidates.unchecked: Number of juntas nationwide, whether there is a recurring report to ARCA, ability to pay (volunteer boards), billing and metering software already used (local competitor search not run), national direction of the Quito fee dispute.

candidates.buyer: Barbershops, hairdressers, spas, small guest houses, child-development centres, sellers of household and public-health pesticides

candidates.existing: None found; competitor search not run.
candidates.known_note: K09 covers Agrocalidad agro-input stores; this is the ARCSA sanitary permit for a different buyer group. K02 uses ARCSA for pharmacy medicine reports.
candidates.name: ARCSA 2026 permit-list roll-out: permit and renewal tracker for newly covered micro-businesses (barbershops, salons, spas, child-care centres, guest houses, pesticide sellers)
candidates.trigger: ARCSA ordered new categories, activities, requirements and fees for operating permits in March 2026, extended implementation to 18 June 2026, and updated the list in August 2026. Base rule is Resolución ARCSA-DE-2023-001-AKRG (Registro Oficial 238, 26 Jan 2023). Many micro-businesses newly need the permit.
candidates.unchecked: Deadlines for the new categories, annual renewal and fees, whether the permit is issued free on ARCSA's portal, how much paperwork (inspection, municipal licence, fire certificate) is repeated, and whether a tracker is just generic reminders. Tattoo studios are not on the list I saw.

candidates.buyer: Households employing domestic or care workers
candidates.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
candidates.existing: Free IESS en Línea portal; calculators and guide sites. No dedicated app seen.
candidates.name: Monthly IESS affiliation, payroll and contribution helper for households employing domestic workers
candidates.trigger: IESS aviso de entrada within 15 days (affiliation from first day), contributions 9.45% worker plus 11.15% employer, minimum wage USD 482 in 2026. Affiliations in the sector fell 4.6% in 2025, so informality is high.
candidates.unchecked: Willingness to pay, how many households actually comply, the 13th/14th-salary and vacation add-ons, local competitor search not run (budget used).

candidates.buyer: Private child-development centres and nurseries (children aged 1-3)
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
candidates.name: Private child-development centre (CDI) annual technical-administrative report and permit file
candidates.trigger: CDI authorisation requires an annual report each August on technical and administrative operation, supervision access, and quality standards. The gob.ec procedure now names the Ministerio de Desarrollo Humano as issuer, but older sources say MIES (unverified which is current).
candidates.unchecked: Current regulator, number of private CDIs, the exact report format, and how it overlaps with the ARCSA permit for early-childhood centres.

candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
candidates.known_note: Same regulator (ANT) as the rejected used-car idea; the bottleneck there was ANT being closed.
candidates.name: Driving-school compliance and course-permit tracker (ANT)
candidates.trigger: Course starts need ANT permits; an administrative intervention from 30 Jan 2026 stopped permit issue and schools in Portoviejo and Manta suspended courses; ANT inspections of schools continued in September 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Whether schools have any recurring periodic report to ANT (I could not find one), and whether the ANT problem is the same closure risk that killed K11.

candidates.buyer: Cattle traders and introducers who sell at municipal camales and fairs
candidates.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
candidates.existing: State SIFAE system (free); no private tool seen.
candidates.name: Livestock introducer and movement-guide helper for cattle traders (SIFAE guía de movilización plus vaccination certificate plus camal introducer code)
candidates.trigger: Cattle entering fairs and camales need a vaccination certificate and a guía de movilización generated in Agrocalidad's SIFAE system; municipal camales require an introducer code. Municipal crackdowns on clandestine slaughter in 2026 (Quito, April) and new ordinance 05-2025.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the guide is issued online for free and quick, and any record-keeping duty beyond each trip. Small and likely low willingness to pay.

candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.known_note: Same buyer group (transport cooperatives); renewal every 10 years is too infrequent. K06 settlement idea is the stronger one.
candidates.name: Operating-permit renewal and SEPS member-list file for taxi and transport cooperatives
candidates.trigger: 10-year municipal operating permit renewal inside a 60-day window before or after expiry, needing a current SEPS member list, legal-representative appointment and ANT tariff payment (USD 282 for cargo cooperatives).

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Employer must file IESS aviso de entrada within 15 days (affiliation from day one) via free IESS en Línea; contributions 9.45% worker plus 11.15% employer on at least the USD 482 basic wage (2026). Domestic-worker affiliations fell 4.6% in 2025, so evasion is common. Only third-party guides and a calculator found, no dedicated app.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No current Ecuadorian dealer-level register or buyer log found. Results were an old COMEXI scrap-exporter register (2007), a public-sector scrapping register (gob.ec), and Argentine and other-country rules. Nothing found to base a candidate on.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers (montes de piedad, casas de empeño) and antique and art dealers became UAFE obligated subjects by a reform published 3 Apr 2023. Same duty and buyer group as K05, so marked known.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Dealers in jewellery, metals and precious stones are UAFE obligated subjects (operations over USD 10,000). Since 10 Sep 2025 the SRI checks this when a RUC is registered or updated; the dealer has 30 business days to get a UAFE code or the RUC is suspended. Covered by K05, so marked known.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Ecuadorian dismantler or used-parts register found (the hits were Argentina's RUDAC). Quito's AMT and the national police are scrapping impounded vehicles, which is a public-sector job and not a candidate. See K11.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Movement guides come from Agrocalidad's SIFAE system and are required for cattle entering markets and camales (vaccination certificate plus guía de movilización). Municipal camales ask introducers to open a code. Agrocalidad and the state run the system free, so only a weak helper idea.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Municipal camal ordinances with fees, a clandestine camal crackdown in Quito (April 2026), and new ordinance 05-2025 in Pedro Vicente Maldonado. Butchers need an ARCSA permit, but I could not confirm 2026 specifics. No national mandatory reporting stream found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: About 2,175 registered producers and 39,430 hives (MAG 2023 catastro). Good-practice guide of 2015. No mandatory recurring report found, so weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Agrocalidad is the competent authority under Andean Decision 483 and registers veterinary-product companies and products (manual dated 2017). I found no clinic-level recurring reporting or traceability duty.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Nothing Ecuador-specific on drillers. Water-use permits need an ARCA certificado de disponibilidad de agua backed by a pumping-test report. Studies describe groundwater management as fragmented. Weak, no candidate.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Hazardous and special-waste gestores and transporters need MAATE authorisation and file an annual declaration (K07, rejected). Non-hazardous waste registers are municipal (example: GAD Rumiñahui). I found no specific procedure for septic or hydro-suction trucks.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Searches returned only Colombia, Spain and Panama. No Ecuador lift, boiler or pressure-vessel rule found. The Quito and Guayaquil fire-brigade ordinances were not checked.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Juntas administradoras de agua potable and saneamiento (community water boards) get legal personality from the environment ministry. ARCA approved a cost guide for water and sanitation tariffs (Registro Oficial 756, March 2025). Quito has 94 juntas and the municipality wants them to collect the waste fee. Candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Agrocalidad registration of agro-input stores is K09 (rejected). New point: ARCSA's 2026 list adds permits for sellers of household, industrial and public-health pesticides (see ARCSA candidate). Applicators were not covered separately.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Outsourcing is limited to complementary activities (security, cleaning, messaging, food, maintenance) under Mandato 8 of 2008. The Ministry of Labour authorises and registers the firms. No 2026 change found. Group B's category 26 covers this.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: ARCSA exempted funeral services and wake rooms (codes 16.0 and 16.1) from the operating permit in 2015, though they stay under sanitary control. Cemeteries are municipal, under the health ministry's cadaver regulation. The 2026 permit list does not mention funerals. Nothing recurring found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: The Ley Orgánica de Transparencia Social (Registro Oficial 28 Aug 2025) and its regulation (Decreto Ejecutivo 191, 27-28 Oct 2025) replace Decreto 193. The SEPS classes foundations and corporations as low, medium or high risk and sets recurring reports for each. This is the strongest new lead and is recorded as a candidate. Halal and kosher supervision is not applicable.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi and operator permits are municipal and renewed every 10 years, with a 60-day window before or after expiry and a SEPS member list required. Cargo operator permit costs USD 282 under the ANT 2026 tariff. ANT services were partly suspended in 2026. The partner-settlement idea is K06.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: RIMPE recategorisation in 2026 (about 14,000 moved from Negocio Popular to Emprendedor per Vistazo; another source says about 70,000, a mismatch). Municipal patent and permit rules vary by canton. No money-changer regime found. Generic tax and accounting work, so out of scope.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: ARCSA widened its permit list in 2026 (Teleamazonas, Aug 2026) to cover barbershops, salons, spas, early-childhood centres, pools, guest houses, bars and pesticide sellers. Driving schools: 182 ANT-authorised schools; an ANT intervention suspended course permits from 30 Jan 2026. Private child-development centres file an annual report each August. No tattoo or hunting rule found.
